items.context: backlog/files.go (292 lines, complexity 35) and initiatives/files.go (312 lines, complexity 35) have 53-57% duplication and are the highest-complexity files. Both implement file upload/download/list for their respective entities. Extracting shared logic is the single highest-leverage refactor.

options.label: Extract to internal/fileserve package
options.rationale: New focused package with generic file-serving helpers (upload, download, list, delete). Both backlog and initiatives call into it. Clean separation, testable in isolation. Recommended because it gives maximum reuse and directly targets both complexity-35 files.

options.label: Extract to existing internal/httputil package
options.rationale: Adds file-serving helpers alongside existing JSON helpers. Fewer new packages but httputil grows in scope and may become a grab-bag.

items.context: emitter.go has 42 functions in 244 lines with 95% duplication. Each method is a thin typed wrapper around a single emit() call. The duplication score is high but the pattern provides compile-time type safety for each event's payload. Consolidating would reduce duplication metrics but may lose that type safety.

options.label: Keep explicit methods, accept duplication score
options.rationale: The current pattern is intentional — each typed method provides compile-time safety and is self-documenting. The 'duplication' is structural, not copy-paste bugs. Touching this doesn't materially improve real code quality.

options.label: Use code generation (go:generate)
options.rationale: Define events in a table, generate the typed wrappers. Reduces maintained lines but adds build complexity and a generation step.

options.label: Consolidate to generic Emit(entityType, entityID, eventType, payload) public API
options.rationale: Callers construct payloads directly. Fewer methods but loses type safety at call sites.

items.context: backlog/encode_error_test.go and queue/encode_error_test.go are 100% identical (39 lines each). Both define the same errorWriter struct and nearly identical test functions. Additionally, settings/helpers_test.go and queue/store_default_test.go share 100% duplication patterns.

options.label: Extract errorWriter to internal/testutil package
options.rationale: Single definition shared across all packages that need it. Eliminates 100% duplication in 4 files. Recommended as it's a clear win with no downsides — testutil already exists in this codebase.

options.label: Keep duplicated per-package (accept score hit)
options.rationale: Go convention often favors test helpers local to the package. Avoids cross-package test dependencies. But with 100% duplication across 4 files, the duplication is clearly wasteful.

items.context: At 472 lines with complexity_max 8 and 67% duplication, this test file has 14 test functions that all follow the same pattern: create item -> build PATCH request -> send -> assert response -> assert saved file. The setup boilerplate is repeated in every test.

options.label: Extract updateTestHelper with common setup/assertion
options.rationale: Create a helper like `doUpdate(t, h, rootDir, kind, name, payload) *httptest.ResponseRecorder` that handles request construction, content-type header, mux vars, and execution. Each test becomes ~5-10 lines of unique logic. Recommended because it directly halves the file length.

options.label: Convert to table-driven tests where possible
options.rationale: Group related tests (e.g., status rejection tests) into table-driven format. Good for the simpler tests but the more complex ones (ChangeDependsOn, SaveItem_PreservesUnknownSpecFields) don't fit neatly into tables.

options.label: Split into multiple test files by concern
options.rationale: E.g., handler_update_status_test.go, handler_update_fields_test.go. Reduces individual file length but doesn't reduce total duplication.

items.text: Only 1 tech debt marker found across the entire swarm-manager API: `api/internal/stats/engine.go:289` — `// TODO: implement follow-up tracking once execution history is available.` This can be removed or converted to a backlog item during cleanup.
acceptance_allow is already set to `scenarios/swarm-manager/**` which correctly covers all planned changes. No acceptance_deny is needed since no sensitive paths exist within this scope.
